method: Compare authored Belarusian sequence/context explanations, 27 definitions/distinctions, 86 reasoning blocks, 44 relations and six complete trails/reflections with the frozen official Belarusian edition and L9.1 local anchors. Stable identities and reference groups follow the accepted model; public prose is separately authored Belarusian, not inherited English editing instructions. Review attribution, agency, causal/conditional links, polarity, certainty, scope and necessary qualifications by source group. Exact quotations are copied only from local contiguous spans. Hashes bind the resulting comparison and do not prove semantic fidelity. No external factual update or native-speaker proofreading is claimed.

standaloneContextReview.renderContract: Source.vue renders buildReadingIndex().paragraphs[].explanation independently. Main sequence prose, placement explanations and optional concept quotations cannot supply missing meaning.

publicCopyReview.scope: All 762 explanatory records, 245 headings/context labels, six complete trails with questions and estimates, and 224 exact source notes.
publicCopyReview.method: Source-context explanations were corrected after root review to state their core substantive argument independently, integrating attributed premises instead of requiring the main explanation or attaching a repeated formula. No main/premise pair is identical. Other main/context records may intentionally share their already complete argument, as in accepted locale patterns. Scenarios are fictional, optional and unscored.

groupReviews.review: The opening keeps construction versus dehumanization, useful/ambivalent technologies, uncertainty, private power, differences and shared action. Local contexts integrate creation, Incarnation, divine wisdom and narrative Nehemiah without performed prayer or a repeated faith suffix. p013 retains the strength/weakness premise and ability-sensitive participation.

Historical contexts retain earthly autonomy, institutional distinction, exceptions that cannot replace civil duties, relevant expertise, open debate, plural cultural expression and Gospel continuity. Truth as gift does not authorize its monopoly. The source of faith claims is explicit.

The chronology preserves worker dignity/association, economic crisis, subsidiarity, legal and international order, human rights, religious freedom, integral development, solidarity, market limits, charity/truth, ecology and fraternity. Later teaching is a developing response, not a proof of automatic institutional innocence.

The four dignity meanings remain distinct; rights are not performance rewards. The universal/inalienable and practical-protection claims coexist with the explicitly attributed conception/natural-death, abortion, killing innocents and euthanasia positions. Manipulated consensus, discrimination and women’s equal dignity remain.

Common good is not summed private benefits. Contribution respects actual abilities. Public/international duties include peoples’ dignity and rejection of subjugation. Property is recognized and subordinated; digital resources, ecology, poor people, future people, waste and exploitation remain. Local p067 wording is used.

Subsidiarity means support/coordination without absorption, expressly rejects State passivity, and applies to dominant private platforms. Audit, transparent algorithms, data access, recourse, public guarantees and prior participation remain. Solidarity is choice, principle and virtue, mutually constraining subsidiarity, with future generations and ecology.

Justice includes structures, restorative action, victims, voice, migrant integration and the right to remain safely at home. Development is every person/whole person. Church self-scrutiny retains real participation, all abuse categories, reparation, prevention, shared goods and corrective evaluation; sacramental premises do not replace accountability.

Local p090 construction imagery replaces an initially too-general free/slave gloss. The technocratic paradigm differs from useful tools. p097–099 scope, obsolescence, limited understanding, computational benefits and attributed categorical anthropological claims stay together. Goals, answerability, challenge, remedies, oversight and value deliberation remain.

Plural enhancement currents are distinguished, with radical forms qualified. Care, relational agency and embodied presence remain. Local p118 says it is right to alleviate suffering, not a duty to eliminate all suffering. n132 heart argument is explained in p120. Fragile institutions and daily fidelity ground practical hope; grace remains distinct from technical self-enhancement.

Truth needs facts, verification and shared trust, not centralized control. Communication forms culture and can normalize war. Journalists’ role and the Church’s independent duty remain. Education needs time, questions, deciding when not to use AI, child safeguards, parental moral/cultural/religious choice, access, pedagogy and intellectual formation.

Work goods exceed income but never confer intrinsic worth. Emergency aid, welcome relief from dangerous tasks, uneven transitions and civic participation without employment remain. Production and finance must be just before redistribution. Local p164’s three actual policy groups are explicit: accountability, inclusive investment, and tax/social/industrial correction.

The attributed man/woman family definition remains, with work/youth stability and the actual p169 work/leisure/rest, learning/retraining and social-network measures. Hidden annotation/training/moderation labor, low pay, women, hazardous child extraction and trafficking channels are attributed to the document. Slavery complicity, delayed condemnation, pardon and present prevention remain explicit. Data copies do not replace decision power.

Hybrid conflict, power culture, militarized interests, memory loss, nuclear thresholds and prolonged conflict are connected. Strict self-defense and last resort remain alongside prohibition of delegated lethal/irreversible decisions, bounded values/sound-judgment work, identifiable/verifiable chains, moral-judgment time, civilian distinction and effective/conscious/responsible control.

Institutional weakness and market faith do not imply inevitable war. Spending costs for poor people, extremism, research duties, unequal personal powers, everyday choices, victim perspective and history/memory distinction remain. Grace is expressly not magical conflict removal. Psalm84 collision is disclosed without assigning Augustine support to n084.

Dialogue does not require agreement or neutrality toward harm. Negotiation, diplomacy, interreligious peace, cyber civilian protection, multilateral reform and mercy’s political role remain. Unarmed/disarming/humble/persevering peace and practical relationships/society survive excluded blessing/prayer forms through separate paraphrase.

Conclusion keeps optional Christian itinerary, Incarnation, sacramental membership and social obligations, active work rather than spiritual retreat, truth/education/presence/hidden labor, narrative prayer, open-city promise and Mary’s perspective under unchanged Roman rule. p244 retains every named vulnerable subject; p245 retains daily sharing. Main/foundation contexts are independently integrated, not repeated appendices.

meaningChecks.p001: Keep the generational choice between humane and dehumanizing construction; put creation and Incarnation behind an attributed foundations link so the secular entry does not imply that these premises are universally accepted.

meaningChecks.p002: Preserve the Church's stated willingness to collaborate with all people in integral development; distinguish this inclusive invitation from its belief that divine action blesses those efforts.

meaningChecks.p003: Locate the present letter in the living social-teaching tradition inaugurated by Rerum Novarum; remove the closing invocation while keeping the argument that proclamation cannot ignore concrete social life.

meaningChecks.p004: Carry forward technology's possible benefits, harms and uncertain long-term effects; separate the appeal to ask God for wisdom from the practical need to interpret current transformations.

meaningChecks.p005: Keep regulation alongside the prior question of who controls technology; private transnational actors exceeding some governments' resources are part of the source's power analysis, not a reason to declare all private activity illegitimate.

meaningChecks.p006: Preserve shared discernment of ends rather than a succession of emergency responses; the open questions ask a community to choose a direction, not predict an inevitable technological future.

meaningChecks.p007: Use Babel as an explicitly biblical interpretation of uniformity and self-assertion, preserving the distinction between coordinated activity and homogenization; do not present the narrative as empirical evidence about AI.

meaningChecks.p008: Retain Nehemiah's listening, distributed work and shared responsibility as the narrative's argumentative work; keep his historical prayer in optional biblical context rather than misclassifying the reported action as a prayer addressed to the reader.

meaningChecks.p009: Preserve both technology's useful possibilities and its dependence on the choices of designers, funders, regulators and users; relocate the Holy Spirit and biblical construction frame without claiming a morally neutral tool.

meaningChecks.p010: Retain the critique of profit that sacrifices the weak and of reducing people to data; explain the two biblical paths as attributed metaphors while preserving plurality as a resource for community.

meaningChecks.p011: Keep the explicit argument that common-good building rests on relationship with God in optional foundations; exclude Augustine's direct prayer without converting the theological desire for fullness into an identical secular claim.

meaningChecks.p012: Keep vulnerability and limits as features of human life rather than failures to erase; progress is evaluated by everyone's dignity and peoples' good, not simply by increased technical capacity.

meaningChecks.p013: Preserve cooperation across institutions and differences, including the claim that tensions can become creative under shared responsibility; collaboration is not an instruction to suppress disagreement.

meaningChecks.p014: Translate the demand for evangelical language into an attributed argument for truthful, non-humiliating communication; retain the institutional tasks of literacy, vulnerable-person protection and guiding research toward justice.

meaningChecks.p015: Use the appeal to remain human amid AI as orientation; keep Jubilee grace and humanity revealed in Christ as foundations rather than treating the ceremony as the source's main policy proposal.

meaningChecks.p016: Retain the call to plan, work and center people ordinarily excluded, while removing the direct prayer and implored blessing clauses; the common-good task must survive those exclusions.

meaningChecks.p017: Provide the chapter's historical-method frame: social teaching develops in dialogue with the sciences and historical change while claiming fidelity to the Gospel; this is the source's account of its development, not proof of unchanging applications.

meaningChecks.p018: Keep the Church's self-description as serving the common good and its distinct relationship to political communities; this explains the institutional speaker before presenting the sequence of popes.

meaningChecks.p019: Preserve the claim that religion cannot be relegated to private life and that the Church may comment on civil events; attribute that public-role claim rather than presenting it as an uncontested rule of politics.

meaningChecks.p020: Keep the acknowledgment of earthly realities' proper autonomy within the Church's theological account; do not erase either autonomy or the belief that the Spirit works within human endeavors.

meaningChecks.p021: Retain the distinction between ecclesiastical and civil responsibilities and the warning that exceptional Church substitutions cannot become normal; this limits institutional scope rather than licensing permanent replacement of public institutions.

meaningChecks.p022: Keep the twofold acknowledgment of earthly autonomy and different spheres of competence as the basis for engagement with sciences and cultures; preserve the Church's own stated purpose in that engagement.

meaningChecks.p023: Retain the welcome offered to sincere seekers of truth, goodness and beauty, with scientific inquiry and diverse expert opinions; do not replace openness to debate with a claim that the Church settles empirical disputes.

meaningChecks.p024: Explain social teaching as discernment developed through Gospel and human knowledge, not a detached list of rules; its criteria concern persons, communities and the common good.

meaningChecks.p025: Keep truth as a shared gift and the warning against monopoly or prestige, including the polyhedron image for multiple perspectives; the source still claims one Gospel truth rather than relativism.

meaningChecks.p026: Preserve cultural and historical plurality in the Church's account of catholicity; local contexts matter to application, even while the text maintains a universal vocation.

meaningChecks.p027: Keep the contrast between a handbook and a living process of discernment, including dialogue, memory and prophecy; do not paraphrase the continuing presence of the Incarnate Word as merely institutional learning.

meaningChecks.p028: Retain the transition to selected stages since Rerum Novarum as a guide to the timeline; do not promise a comprehensive history beyond the overview the author supplies.

meaningChecks.p029: Preserve the distinction between ancient Gospel reception and its modern systematization; the source does not describe social doctrine as spontaneously invented in the modern age.

meaningChecks.p030: Keep Rerum Novarum's worker dignity, association and wage concerns as the historical starting point; preserve its claim that evangelization has structural consequences rather than replacing it with a purely economic origin story.

meaningChecks.p031: Retain Quadragesima Anno's criticism of both unlimited competition and collectivist suppression of personal responsibility, together with association and fair remuneration; the paired criticism prevents a one-sided political summary.

meaningChecks.p032: Keep Pius XII's war-and-reconstruction context, law over force, intermediary organizations and international imbalances; this is an attributed historical account, not a claim that all those institutions worked as intended.

meaningChecks.p033: Preserve John XXIII's widening global focus and rights-based institutions and relations between peoples; do not reduce the development to a change of papal personnel.

meaningChecks.p034: Retain Vatican II's turning point, human dignity and pluralistic peaceful societies; the historical explanation must keep the concrete rights criteria rather than just celebratory Council language.

meaningChecks.p035: Keep Paul VI's account of peace as more than the absence of war, linked to humane development and poorer countries; do not treat economic growth alone as the definition of peace.

meaningChecks.p036: Preserve Octogesima Adveniens' engagement with postindustrial change and exclusion; the historical application requires that no person or people be treated as expendable.

meaningChecks.p037: Retain John Paul II's treatment of work amid ideological crisis, sufficient remuneration and participation; labor's personal dignity is more than its usefulness to production.

meaningChecks.p038: Keep underdevelopment, responsibility and solidarity in Sollicitudo Rei Socialis; preserve the connection to political charity and civilization of love as the source's normative frame.

meaningChecks.p040: Keep Benedict XVI's widening of development and the political community's irreplaceable responsibility; this limits a reading in which growth alone or private generosity supplies the common good.

meaningChecks.p041: Preserve charity joined to truth and its critical public role; the text does not define charity as private sentiment detached from institutions or justice.

meaningChecks.p042: Keep Francis' account of history through hopes and vulnerabilities and the Church's learning from the poor; the poor are participants in the institution's transformation, not merely recipients.

meaningChecks.p043: Retain integral ecology and the criticism of self-referential politics and finance in Laudato Si'; preserve the source's systemic connection between environmental and social harms.

meaningChecks.p044: Keep Fratelli Tutti's response to fragmentation, conflict and pandemic in the account of fraternity; its broad social friendship must not be narrowed to the author's own religious group.

meaningChecks.p045: Retain the conclusion that social teaching responds to concrete history while preserving an internal core; the overview invites attention to coherence, not a claim that no historical tensions exist.

meaningChecks.p046: Introduce the principles as interrelated within a living teaching in dialogue with history, cultures and sciences; individual concept cards must not imply that each principle stands alone.

meaningChecks.p047: Preserve the different responsibilities of lay people and pastoral leaders for just social life; identify the original religious audience while making the duties legible without silently changing who is addressed.

meaningChecks.p048: Keep the Trinity as the stated source of received and shared love in optional foundations; it is a theological premise, not another name for interpersonal cooperation.

meaningChecks.p049: Preserve the Incarnation and Spirit-led life as the Christian grounding of social consequences; moving this explanation to foundations must not imply that the ethical claims had no religious basis.

meaningChecks.p050: Keep being created in God's image as the source's account of personhood and the person as the Church's way; retain that rationale separately from the secular statement of unconditional worth.

meaningChecks.p059: Keep the move from inalienable personal dignity to obligations toward society; contributing within one's ability protects participation without demanding identical capacity from everyone.

meaningChecks.p060: Use the Council's definition of social conditions enabling fulfillment for groups and individuals; retain the common good's moral dimension rather than presenting it as aggregate convenience.

meaningChecks.p061: Keep the whole's surplus over a sum of interests as an argument about shared life; do not turn the metaphor of a plus into a calculable metric or disregard individual persons.

meaningChecks.p062: Retain a people as a living reality formed through a shared vision and agreements; participation and differences remain part of that vision rather than enforced unanimity.

meaningChecks.p063: Preserve the State's responsibility for cohesion and effective participation, including the credibility lost through corruption and exclusion; common-good rhetoric must be tested against institutional conduct.

meaningChecks.p118: Retain the explicit legitimacy of alleviating suffering alongside acceptance of finitude; the religious interpretation belongs in foundations, and no adaptation may imply that suffering should be left untreated.

meaningChecks.p119: Keep compassion and the possibility of wisdom and closeness amid loss and failure; divine presence and worship are the source's additional religious interpretation, not a guarantee that suffering improves everyone.

meaningChecks.p120: Preserve the author's strong philosophical claim about suffering, love and desire as an attributed argument; connect it to the neighboring permission to relieve suffering rather than presenting it as clinical advice.

meaningChecks.p121: Keep moral evil, possible conversion and Frankl's contrast between perpetrators and victims; the historical reference to prayer is not a prayer to remove, and hope must not excuse atrocity.

meaningChecks.p122: Preserve vulnerability as a possible opening to fraternity and art's resistance to normalized evil; keep the named works as interpretive examples, not evidence that all audiences react alike.

meaningChecks.p123: Retain history's institutional achievements in protecting people as well as its violence; present their fragility and the responsibility to sustain them rather than inevitable moral improvement.

meaningChecks.p124: Keep particular movements and witnesses of human dignity as examples of change; the selected figures illustrate the source's claim and are not a complete or uniform account of world history.

meaningChecks.p125: Preserve hidden service and perseverance alongside public witnesses, with religious communities and named believers as actual examples; do not turn credible witness into a purely technological mechanism of progress.

meaningChecks.p126: Keep the welcome for progress that relieves suffering on condition it preserves relationship and love; distinguish this practical condition from the Christian answer locating fulfillment in grace.

meaningChecks.p127: Keep the account of self-transcendence through divine gift and the Spirit, including Aquinas' disparity between created nature and divine life; secular self-improvement is not an equivalent paraphrase of grace.

meaningChecks.p128: Keep grace and communion as theological premises while retaining the contrast between algorithmic correction and a person's possible transformation through error; the person's future is not to be treated as exhausted by a prediction.

meaningChecks.p129: Preserve Christian humanism's welcome for science under common-good and care criteria, with both conditional outcomes of technological progress; neither automatic optimism nor blanket fear represents the text.

meaningChecks.p130: Use Augustine's two loves as an attributed moral interpretation of personal and institutional priorities; preserve the inward challenge without confusing two cities with a geographic or partisan division.

meaningChecks.p131: Keep the three announced application areas together: truth in public life, work's dignity and freedom from dependence and commercialization; the chapter is broader than employment alone.

meaningChecks.p132: Preserve the double potential of platforms and AI for dialogue and manipulation; factual veracity is proposed as a common good necessary to just communication.

meaningChecks.p133: Keep resource-rich actors' influence over opinion and the need to pursue truth; the source diagnoses concentrated communicative power rather than claiming that all mediated opinion is fabricated.

meaningChecks.p134: Retain truth's enabling role in democracy and the warning about losing distinctions between fact and fiction; do not convert this into a demand that everyone share a political opinion.

meaningChecks.p135: Keep communication as cultural formation rather than information transfer alone; the online world affects lived relationships and imagination, especially among young people.

meaningChecks.p136: Preserve platform power over collective imagination and the positive goal of inner freedom and critical thought; a communication environment can nurture rather than dominate readers.

meaningChecks.p137: Keep the refusal both to demonize and idolize tools, joined to verification and understanding complexity; responsible use requires intellectual formation beyond a checklist of apps.

meaningChecks.p138: Preserve journalists' role in exposing Church abuse and the institution's duty to confront uncomfortable facts without external compulsion; do not sanitize the source's shame or transfer responsibility to reporters.

meaningChecks.p139: Keep education's importance amid manipulation and the fatigue that discourages seeking truth; distinguish the diagnosed pressures from an assertion that young people are inherently incapable of thought.

meaningChecks.p140: Preserve patient engagement with reality and the warning that convenient AI answers can make thinking seem unnecessary; do not state that every use of AI blocks learning.

meaningChecks.p141: Retain the source's concerns about early unsupervised exposure, bullying and sensitive images with source date and attribution; its appeal to literature is not a substitute for current clinical guidance or a universal diagnosis.

meaningChecks.p142: Keep parents' limited ability to resist attention markets and the need for shared safeguards and literacy; assigning the whole duty to families would change the passage's institutional agency.

meaningChecks.p143: Preserve school as a place for truth, life questions and dignity across cultural and religious convictions; education is not a test of conformity to the encyclical's beliefs.

meaningChecks.p144: Retain inequalities in educational access and the duty to make schooling accessible regardless of family resources; the socio-political challenge must remain visible beside pedagogical concerns.

meaningChecks.p145: Keep the pedagogical challenge of integral formation and critical, creative use of technology; catching up with devices is not the same as educating a person.

meaningChecks.p146: Preserve intellectual discipline, reading and careful analysis as conditions for inner freedom; do not promise an effortless atlas that replaces the intellectual work the text values.

meaningChecks.p147: Keep the shared educational alliance among families, schools, Christian communities and public institutions; retain time and trustworthy relationships as things technology alone cannot supply.

meaningChecks.p148: Keep work's protected dignity and its capacity for shared achievement; Benedict's union of prayer and work is historical religious context, not a liturgical formula to delete.

meaningChecks.p149: Preserve work's personal value and the allowance for emergency financial assistance; the limitation concerns aid as the sole response, not condemnation of every form of income support.

meaningChecks.p150: Keep promised productivity alongside possible deskilling, surveillance and lost agency; the criticism concerns current approaches and risks, not an assertion that automation always worsens every job.

meaningChecks.p151: Retain unemployment's serious consequences and State responsibility, with contraction fears limited to some contexts; do not present the passage as a quantitative forecast of global job losses.

meaningChecks.p152: Keep technological relief from arduous and dangerous tasks as desirable while preserving employment and the person as an end; the general protection rule is not an absolute ban on changing any job.

meaningChecks.p153: Preserve uneven transitions, different regional effects and the lack of a universal solution; adaptive local and national responses are central, not a footnote to a single global prescription.

meaningChecks.p154: Keep work's relational and civic roles, but also the duty to rethink citizenship where work diminishes so unemployment does not remove social participation; human worth must not become conditional on employment.

meaningChecks.p155: Retain organized responses from social teaching and the duty to prevent people being stranded among replacement machines; historical efforts are the basis for present institution-building rather than nostalgia for an unchanged labor market.

meaningChecks.p156: Keep anticipation of transformation, formation and dignified new work before jobs disappear; a purely reactive unemployment response loses the preventive agency of the passage.

meaningChecks.p157: Preserve economic activity's service to society and the creation of valuable jobs; business success is evaluated through its social contribution rather than exempted from responsibility.

meaningChecks.p158: Keep the contrast between proclaimed economic freedom and conditions preventing people from benefiting; promised automatic prosperity is criticized through its burdens on those with least power.

meaningChecks.p159: Retain the challenge to GDP-centered metrics and the broader goods named, including peace through justice; the text does not supply a ready-made alternative numerical index.

meaningChecks.p160: Preserve the distinction between finance for productive development and speculative pursuits, including the discussion of cryptocurrencies; do not make every financial innovation synonymous with speculation.

meaningChecks.p161: Keep concentration of growing wealth and access to innovation's benefits, including care and knowledge; absolute aggregate growth alone does not answer distributive justice.

meaningChecks.p162: Retain redistributive laws and fair taxation while keeping justice throughout acquisition, financing, production and consumption; redistribution after production cannot absolve unjust processes.

meaningChecks.p163: Keep political responsibility beyond reliance on an invisible hand, with widespread inclusive sustainable prosperity; the passage does not propose that all market activity should cease.

meaningChecks.p164: Preserve the concrete economy-and-AI criteria that make innovation humane, especially accountable decisions and fair opportunities; their role is to civilize innovation rather than oppose it as such.

meaningChecks.p165: Preserve the source's definition of family as an enduring union of a man and a woman with explicit attribution, alongside its social-good claim; do not silently broaden that definition or present it as uncontested consensus.

meaningChecks.p166: Retain the family's fragility under changing work and the contrast between celebrated technical success and eroding social stability; this is an institutional effect, not blame placed on individual households.

meaningChecks.p167: Keep youth insecurity and the conditions for long-term commitments, with unpredictable economic risks; hope here requires more than encouragement to be confident.

meaningChecks.p168: Preserve the State's role in conditions for employment and protection during transition; supporting businesses is linked to people at the center rather than an unconditional benefit to firms.

meaningChecks.p169: Keep concrete policies making stability feasible for families and young people; technological change is to be evaluated against capacity to build a future, not only immediate output.

meaningChecks.p170: Preserve dependencies, digital sobriety and protection of minors against exploitative models; distinguish responsibility for environments from treating vulnerable users as solely at fault.

meaningChecks.p171: Keep profiling and mass data collection as possible social control and the duty to safeguard conscience; the risk diagnosis is not a claim that every data use is surveillance.

meaningChecks.p172: Retain the criticism of treating a person as a manipulable object and its connection to tolerated subordination; freedom concerns a view of persons as well as the presence of technical controls.

meaningChecks.p173: Keep the digital economy's material and labor dependencies and the argument that efficiency cannot excuse subordination; no adaptation may describe digital products as immaterial or labor-free.

meaningChecks.p174: Retain new slavery as a decisive test of AI ethics and the warning about condemning old harms while tolerating new ones; advanced technology is not evidence of moral advancement.

meaningChecks.p175: Keep trafficking as grave violation and the insistence on firm response; do not reduce organized exploitation to unfortunate side effects of otherwise efficient markets.

meaningChecks.p176: Retain historical caution, Church slave ownership and legitimation, long tolerance before condemnation, eighteen centuries, and institutional pardon. Flag the local sentence that says society and Church condemned slavery without the delay qualifier; do not repair it inside a quotation or let it erase the paragraph’s explicit later admission.

meaningChecks.p177: Retain the move from admitted complicity to present prevention, protection, liberation and rehabilitation; religious responsibility motivates concrete action rather than replacing it with retrospective regret.

meaningChecks.p178: Keep the author's analysis of colonial data extraction, including health and genetic information, and people's power to decide use and benefit; returning copies of data alone would not meet the demand.

meaningChecks.p179: Preserve the distinct responsibilities of supply chains, investors, platforms, authorities and civil society; transparency, due diligence and victim protection must not collapse into a vague shared duty.

meaningChecks.p180: Keep the integration of truth, education, work, family and freedom into one development test; technical capacity requires a wise perspective to become growth, justice and fraternity.

meaningChecks.p181: Retain foresight, shared responsibilities and the inviolable dignity of every person as the measure of authentic progress; efficiency is not an independent exemption from that measure.

meaningChecks.p182: Preserve the chapter's turn to war as a test of moral maturity, particularly for governors; do not disperse responsibility so widely that those directing conflict disappear.

meaningChecks.p183: Keep cyberattacks, information and hybrid conflict alongside conventional warfare; the same social principles still guide decision-making across the changed forms of conflict.

meaningChecks.p184: Explain the contrast between domination and rebuilding through the prior biblical images; retain common-good construction as the substantive alternative and label the metaphors' religious origin.

meaningChecks.p185: Keep the diagnosis of polarization and violence together with civilization of love as an active construction site; hope is a program of work, not denial of the conflicts named.

meaningChecks.p186: Retain Paul VI's Cold War origin of civilization of love and the move from armed coexistence to a shared future; historical context prevents the phrase from becoming a slogan without institutional meaning.

meaningChecks.p187: Keep digital proximity as an opportunity requiring mutual care and rights and duties; network connection is not already a community with a shared future.

meaningChecks.p188: Preserve power's agenda-setting effects, weakening multilateralism and the claimed inevitability of force; that inevitability is the position criticized, not the author's conclusion.

meaningChecks.p189: Keep the historical call against war and the postwar effort to avoid another world war; distinguish the remembered aspiration from any claim that intervening conflicts did not occur.

meaningChecks.p190: Retain the source's diagnosis of normalization of war and rearmament in discourse, including algorithmic amplification of conflict; date and attribute this contemporary diagnosis instead of treating it as timeless data.

meaningChecks.p191: Keep the loss of witnesses to the Holocaust and World Wars and its implications for judgments by power alone; historical memory informs responsibility without substituting for present facts.

meaningChecks.p192: Preserve the contribution of fragmented communication to hostility and civilian suffering; avoid claiming one algorithm alone causes war or that communication is detached from material violence.

meaningChecks.p193: Keep financial and industrial interests that can fuel conflict in the author's diagnosis; do not infer an unproved motive for every individual involved in military production.

meaningChecks.p194: Retain concern about renewed arsenals and miniaturized weapons making use seem more viable; apparent usability does not reduce the destructive ethical stakes.

meaningChecks.p195: Keep weak diplomacy, complex interests and the asymmetry between starting and stopping war; preserve prevention as the neglected task rather than assuming every dispute has an immediate easy settlement.

meaningChecks.p196: Retain non-state armed groups and conflict sustained as a source of power or income; this complicates an account in which every conflict seeks a conventional final victory.

meaningChecks.p197: Preserve the Holy See's last-resort legitimate-self-defense condition and rigorous limits on AI weapons; do not turn the paragraph into either endorsement of autonomous violence or an unqualified claim that no force is ever permitted.

meaningChecks.p198: Keep the prohibition on delegating lethal or irreversible decisions and the rejection of calculable moral judgment; preserve the additional permission to instill values and boundaries in systems rather than claiming ethics work is pointless.

meaningChecks.p199: Retain the three concrete criteria: traceable personal responsibility, time for moral judgment and protection of civilians; speed must not displace judgment in irreversible war decisions.

meaningChecks.p200: Keep reconstructable decision chains, effective self-aware human control and shared international safeguards; a nominal human button alone is not the control described by the author.

meaningChecks.p201: Preserve the crisis of institutions for a common future and mistrust among multiple powers; the passage criticizes conflict-ridden multipolarity rather than claiming one pole should dominate.

meaningChecks.p202: Keep enemy-based identity and narratives that bypass institutions, with consequences for cohesion; do not reproduce the good-versus-evil binary as the atlas's own categorization of peoples.

meaningChecks.p203: Preserve the displacement of development, disarmament and prevention, including civilian and child protection; describing those goods as naïve is the attitude being criticized.

meaningChecks.p204: Keep the costs of militarization borne by the poorest through reduced health, education and services; practical resource consequences must remain beside the critique of spiritual blindness.

meaningChecks.p205: Preserve the rejection of false realism and peace as the possible fruit of justice and charity; possibility is not a promise that every negotiation will succeed.

meaningChecks.p206: Retain the criticism of religious extremism and identity fanaticism alongside nihilistic pragmatism; religious language here carries self-critical moral analysis rather than a devotional formula.

meaningChecks.p207: Keep the warning about hollow rights, unresolved resentments and renewed aggression; the risks are grounded in social conditions rather than an inevitable cycle attributed to every victim.

meaningChecks.p208: Preserve the open question of concrete safeguards and the critique of war used to divert domestic attention; identify the mechanism without inventing examples of named governments.

meaningChecks.p209: Keep researchers, businesses and institutions responsible for critical assessment of projects and their possible complicity; ignorance cannot automatically absolve participation in harmful systems.

meaningChecks.p210: Retain the naming of perpetual conflict as evil and the invitation to change its direction; distinguish Isaiah's theological hope from evidence that improvement is guaranteed.

meaningChecks.p211: Keep witnesses who persist in the darkest periods as grounds for the source's theological hope; preserve that religious account without converting it to a forecast of inevitable historical progress.

meaningChecks.p212: Keep everyday choices of truth, moderation and care as meaningful contributions, without claiming they alone solve large institutional conflicts; small agency coexists with public duties.

meaningChecks.p213: Use Tolkien's cited line as a literary illustration of responsibility within one's time, with the subsequent practical routes to peace; do not present a fictional character's words as empirical evidence.

meaningChecks.p214: Retain words' capacity to inflame or disarm, including denunciation of injustice and support for excluded voices; peaceful language must not mean silence about harm.

meaningChecks.p215: Keep justice as peace's foundation and reject mere domination or an enforced pause as sufficient peace; preserve the demand for a specific kind of peace, not stability at any price. The frozen [84] is inside Psalm 85 [84], not evidence that n084 supplies the Augustine quotation; preserve its stored backlink but disclose this visible numbering collision.

meaningChecks.p216: Retain the claim that neutrality can be unjust in some conflicts, with history and memory serving different roles; neither side-taking in every dispute nor erasing witnesses follows from the paragraph.

meaningChecks.p217: Keep victims' voices in communication and education as an appeal against evil and toward peace; recognizing suffering is not permission to cultivate revenge or new conflicts.

meaningChecks.p218: Preserve healthy realism's rejection of both purity that ignores conditions and cynicism that normalizes evil; verifiable guarantees, negotiation, prevention and civilian protection make the distinction practical.

meaningChecks.p219: Keep dialogue as the primary means of coexistence and the possibility of honorable solutions through perseverance; do not turn the claimed possibility into assurance of an easy settlement.

meaningChecks.p220: Retain ordinary listening to strangers and migrants as part of peacebuilding beyond State diplomacy; distinct everyday and political scales should remain intelligible.

meaningChecks.p221: Keep the political shift toward a culture of negotiation as a patient ethical and cultural commitment; diplomacy is a practice with time and institutions, not simply nicer speech.

meaningChecks.p222: Preserve the author's appeal to governors to reject a mindset dividing the world into the good and evil; attribution is essential when summarizing the quoted papal address.

meaningChecks.p223: Keep interreligious dialogue and the rejection of sanctified hatred, naming religious traditions as actors; this religious discussion is substantive peacebuilding rather than prayer to omit.

meaningChecks.p224: Preserve diplomacy's preventive and trust-building role, including attention to faint signs of goodwill; uncertainty and patience belong to the argument rather than a promised immediate result.

meaningChecks.p225: Keep cyberattacks, manipulation and AI-assisted influence as real violence requiring protection and international arrangements; invisibility does not make harms imaginary or exempt civilian interests.

meaningChecks.p226: Retain the importance of the United Nations and other international organizations together with the distortions and divisions that impede them; institutional support is not a claim that they are already sufficient or beyond criticism.

meaningChecks.p227: Preserve the Holy See's adoption of mercy as a diplomatic criterion and its concrete service to common-good peacebuilding; label the Gospel premise while avoiding a generic claim that diplomacy has no political consequences.

meaningChecks.p228: Keep the commitment to achieve peace in relationships and society and the attributed religious account of hope; exclude the repeated blessing and direct calls to pray, never the practical responsibility attached to them.

meaningChecks.p229: Retain the conclusion's careful-building and unity frame as the outline of a Christian program; separate prayer and ceremonial address from substantive common-good construction and contextual sacramental premises.

meaningChecks.p230: Keep the critique of disguised control of markets and influence alongside the religious alternative of mercy; the Magnificat functions as a theological interpretive frame, not evidence that the market diagnosis is scientifically established.

meaningChecks.p231: Keep attention to children, elderly people, victims and human struggle within the Incarnation argument; move its explicit theological grounding to foundations and remove the Lord's Prayer formula without losing vulnerable persons.

meaningChecks.p232: Preserve the Incarnation's alternative to disembodied enhancement, including the acknowledged yearning for fuller life; exclude the devotional exclamation while retaining the doctrinal claim that divine love shares human fragility.

meaningChecks.p233: Keep the call to responsible participation and the human face at the center, with consciousness claims attributed; preserve recapitulation in Christ as an optional theological promise rather than secular technological prediction.

meaningChecks.p234: Keep Eucharistic communion as the stated origin of Christian solidarity; remove Augustine's recited response sequence while retaining his argument about membership and unity, not merely deleting the whole sacramental explanation.

meaningChecks.p235: Preserve the Church's duty to share, oppose exclusion and give voice to invisible people; remove the opening liturgical response while keeping Eucharistic rationale in foundations rather than replacing it with secular individual piety.

meaningChecks.p236: Keep active responsibility, human limitations and the four closing commitments, with rejection of retreat into spiritual sentimentality; preserve the Kingdom and Christ imagery as attributed foundations.

meaningChecks.p237: Retain resistance to manipulative information, situated relationships and care for the common home; keep revealed truth about God and humanity as the source's premise rather than a rule that readers must profess faith.

meaningChecks.p238: Keep patient adult formation, shared partnerships and young people's inner freedom; label evangelization as the Church's distinct vocation and do not turn the educational main path into a religious agreement test.

meaningChecks.p239: Retain physical presence, meals, care for lonely people and service to the poor amid digital connection; preserve the body's theological meaning without implying every digital relationship lacks authenticity.

meaningChecks.p240: Keep supply-chain examination, hidden work and business models profiting from manipulation or war alongside practical fairness and participation; separate Christ-grounded hope from the concrete ethical tasks.

meaningChecks.p241: Retain Nehemiah's organized rebuilding as an attributed parable for laboratories, companies, schools and communities; report the narrative prayer as context and separate the reader's exhortation to prayer from present responsibility.

meaningChecks.p242: Preserve Revelation's city as a promised gift with open gates and healing, and its call to overcome divisions; this eschatological image is not a secular infrastructure plan or an excuse to drop cooperation.

meaningChecks.p243: Keep the distinction between unchanged oppression and a changed perspective, and the claim that God sides with the lowly; remove the performed hymn of praise while retaining its theological and political interpretation in context.

meaningChecks.p244: Preserve the explicit invitation to read history through sufferers, widows, orphans, strangers and displaced people; Marian framing goes to foundations, never into a whole-paragraph devotional omission that would erase these perspectives.

meaningChecks.p245: Keep sharing oneself and one's goods through everyday fidelity as the substantive closing task; exclude the final entrustment to Mary while preserving Incarnation and salvation-history claims as optional foundations rather than secular guarantees.

meaningChecks.p051: Preserve the transition from uniqueness and dignity to rights inherent in being human; the authority cited is John Paul II and the Church's teaching, not an unqualified legal claim about every jurisdiction.

sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Леў XIV ставіць кожнае пакаленне перад выбарам: абараняць годнасць, справядлівасць і братэрства або будаваць яшчэ больш бесчалавечны свет. Веліч праекта сама па сабе не вызначае яго чалавечай каштоўнасці.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve the Church's stated willingness to collaborate with all people in integral development; distinguish this inclusive invitation from its belief that divine action blesses those efforts.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Аўтар прапануе супрацоўнічаць з усімі, хто імкнецца да больш справядлівага свету. Дыялог патрэбны для пошуку шляхоў развіцця кожнага чалавека, а не толькі для абвяшчэння гатовых адказаў.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Locate the present letter in the living social-teaching tradition inaugurated by Rerum Novarum; remove the closing invocation while keeping the argument that proclamation cannot ignore concrete social life.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Сацыяльнае вучэнне Касцёла прадстаўлена як традыцыя распазнавання, а не нерухомы набор адказаў. Яно спалучае прынцыпы, ацэнку канкрэтных абставінаў і напрамкі дзеяння.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Carry forward technology's possible benefits, harms and uncertain long-term effects; separate the appeal to ask God for wisdom from the practical need to interpret current transformations.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Тэхналогіі могуць паляпшаць жыццё, але іх магутнасць уплывае на рашэнні і калектыўнае ўяўленне. Хуткасць перамен не дазваляе цалкам прадказаць доўгатэрміновыя наступствы для годнасці і агульнага дабра.
qualificationChecks: Тэхналогіі могуць паляпшаць жыццё, але іх магутнасць уплывае на рашэнні і калектыўнае ўяўленне. Хуткасць перамен не дазваляе цалкам прадказаць доўгатэрміновыя наступствы для годнасці і агульнага дабра. Пераасэнсоўваючы заклік Льва XIII, аўтар звязвае патрэбу ў Божай мудрасці з распазнаваннем тэхналагічных тэндэнцый. Тэхналогіі належаць чалавечай гісторыі і могуць паляпшаць жыццё, але іх карысць суіснуе з рызыкай шкоды. Лічбавізацыя, ШІ і робататэхніка ўплываюць на рашэнні і ўяўленне; магутнасць і хуткасць змен ускладняюць прагноз іх наступстваў для годнасці і агульнага дабра.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep regulation alongside the prior question of who controls technology; private transnational actors exceeding some governments' resources are part of the source's power analysis, not a reason to declare all private activity illegitimate.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Правілы неабходныя, але самі не вырашаюць пытання пра мэты тэхналогій. Кампаніі, здольныя ўплываць мацней за некаторыя ўрады, робяць уладу менш відавочнай і цяжэйшай для грамадскага кантролю.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve shared discernment of ends rather than a succession of emergency responses; the open questions ask a community to choose a direction, not predict an inevitable technological future.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Неадкладныя задачы не павінны засланяць культурных і духоўных каранёў перамен. Сумеснае распазнаванне пачынаецца з пытанняў пра мэту развіцця і будучыню, якую людзі хочуць будаваць разам.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Use Babel as an explicitly biblical interpretation of uniformity and self-assertion, preserving the distinction between coordinated activity and homogenization; do not present the narrative as empirical evidence about AI.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Бабілёнская вежа паказвае спакусу адзінства праз панаванне і аднастайнасць. У гэтай логіцы годнасць можа стаць ахвярай эфектыўнасці, а чалавецтва — уласнай прэтэнзіі на самадастатковасць.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain Nehemiah's listening, distributed work and shared responsibility as the narrative's argumentative work; keep his historical prayer in optional biblical context rather than misclassifying the reported action as a prayer addressed to the reader.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Аповед пра Нээмію паказвае іншы спосаб будаваць: пачуць боль разбуранага горада, арганізаваць працу і даць кожнаму месца. Агульная мова не патрабуе аднолькавасці ўсіх удзельнікаў.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve both technology's useful possibilities and its dependence on the choices of designers, funders, regulators and users; relocate the Holy Spirit and biblical construction frame without claiming a morally neutral tool.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Навуковыя адкрыцці могуць служыць аднаўленню сумеснага жыцця або ўмацаванню панавання. Пытанне датычыць таго, дзеля чаго людзі арганізуюць тэхналагічную магутнасць і каго ўключаюць у яе карысць.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain the critique of profit that sacrifices the weak and of reducing people to data; explain the two biblical paths as attributed metaphors while preserving plurality as a resource for community.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Прыбытак не можа апраўдаць ахвяраванне слабымі, а агульная мова — сціранне адрозненняў. Чалавека нельга звесці да лічбавага кода ці функцыі вытворчасці.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep the explicit argument that common-good building rests on relationship with God in optional foundations; exclude Augustine's direct prayer without converting the theological desire for fullness into an identical secular claim.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: У хрысціянскім разуменні аўтара жаданне шчасця ахоплівае ўсё жыццё і накіравана да адносінаў з Богам. Ён звязвае агульнае дабро з такой адкрытасцю; дыялог Касцёла са светам павінен захоўваць і накіроўваць гэтае імкненне.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep vulnerability and limits as features of human life rather than failures to erase; progress is evaluated by everyone's dignity and peoples' good, not simply by increased technical capacity.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Паўната жыцця не роўная бясконцай тэхнічнай дасканаласці. Аўтар прапануе прыняць чалавечую слабасць і звязаць свабоду з адказнасцю, узаемным клопатам і салідарнасцю.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve cooperation across institutions and differences, including the claim that tensions can become creative under shared responsibility; collaboration is not an instruction to suppress disagreement.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Ніхто не здольны адзін несці ўсе выклікі, але ніхто не настолькі слабы, каб нічога не ўнесці. Сумесная адказнасць можа ператварыць адрозненні ў крыніцу творчага супрацоўніцтва.
qualificationChecks: Ніхто не здольны адзін несці ўсе выклікі, але ніхто не настолькі слабы, каб нічога не ўнесці. Сумесная адказнасць можа ператварыць адрозненні ў крыніцу творчага супрацоўніцтва. Сумесная адказнасць пачынаецца з двух сцвярджэнняў: ніхто не можа адзін несці ўсе выклікі і ніхто не настолькі слабы, каб не ўнесці нічога. Біблійная думка пра сілу ў слабасці падтрымлівае гэты заклік. Аўтар дае розным прафесіям і супольнасцям свой участак працы; субсідыярнасць і супрацоўніцтва могуць ператварыць напружанасць у творчасць без патрабавання ад усіх аднолькавай моцы.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Translate the demand for evangelical language into an attributed argument for truthful, non-humiliating communication; retain the institutional tasks of literacy, vulnerable-person protection and guiding research toward justice.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Яснасць і шчырасць павінны дапамагаць распазнаваць перамены, а не зняважваць людзей, палохаць або ўхваляць тэхналогіі без крытыкі. Арыенціры — годнасць, агульныя даброты, бедныя, навакольнае асяроддзе і мір.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Use the appeal to remain human amid AI as orientation; keep Jubilee grace and humanity revealed in Christ as foundations rather than treating the ceremony as the source's main policy proposal.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Тэхнічная моц не замяняе адкрытага сэрца, слухання і волі да еднасці. Перад складанымі задачамі патрэбны не толькі новыя сродкі, але і людзі, гатовыя супрацоўнічаць.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain the call to plan, work and center people ordinarily excluded, while removing the direct prayer and implored blessing clauses; the common-good task must survive those exclusions.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Аўтар заклікае да планавання, настойлівай працы і супрацоўніцтва з беднымі, хворымі, мігрантамі і іншымі адкінутымі людзьмі. Яны павінны быць удзельнікамі агульнага дому, а не матэрыялам чужога праекта.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Provide the chapter's historical-method frame: social teaching develops in dialogue with the sciences and historical change while claiming fidelity to the Gospel; this is the source's account of its development, not proof of unchanging applications.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Гісторыя сацыяльнага вучэння паказвае яго дынамічны характар. Новыя падзеі патрабуюць не толькі прымянення ранейшых катэгорый, але і іх пераасэнсавання; для аўтара такое развіццё павінна захоўваць вернасць Евангеллю.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep the Church's self-description as serving the common good and its distinct relationship to political communities; this explains the institutional speaker before presenting the sequence of popes.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Каб зразумець унёсак асобных Папаў, аўтар спачатку тлумачыць адносіны Касцёла са светам. Ён прызнае аўтаномію зямных рэалій і адрознівае эклезіяльную супольнасць ад палітычнай; служэнне агульнаму дабру не азначае іх зліцця.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve the claim that religion cannot be relegated to private life and that the Church may comment on civil events; attribute that public-role claim rather than presenting it as an uncontested rule of politics.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Касцёл бачыць сваю місію ў слуханні, дыялогу і служэнні чалавечай сям’і. Рэлігійнае сведчанне, паводле аўтара, мае сацыяльныя наступствы, але павінна ўваходзіць у рэальнае жыццё людзей, а не замяняць яго абстрактнай схемай.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep the acknowledgment of earthly realities' proper autonomy within the Church's theological account; do not erase either autonomy or the belief that the Spirit works within human endeavors.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Зямныя рэаліі маюць уласную вартасць і заканамернасці. Аўтар прызнае іх аўтаномію разам са сваёй верай у дзеянне Духа ў гісторыі; падтрымка чалавечай адказнасці не азначае рэлігійнага прысваення кожнага грамадскага рашэння.
qualificationChecks: Зямныя рэаліі маюць уласную вартасць і заканамернасці. Аўтар прызнае іх аўтаномію разам са сваёй верай у дзеянне Духа ў гісторыі; падтрымка чалавечай адказнасці не азначае рэлігійнага прысваення кожнага грамадскага рашэння.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain the distinction between ecclesiastical and civil responsibilities and the warning that exceptional Church substitutions cannot become normal; this limits institutional scope rather than licensing permanent replacement of public institutions.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Другі Ватыканскі Сабор адрознівае палітычную і эклезіяльную супольнасці. Аўтар дапускае дапамогу ў надзвычайных абставінах, але яна не можа стаць пастаяннай заменай грамадзянскіх інстытутаў і іх уласнай адказнасці.
qualificationChecks: Другі Ватыканскі Сабор адрознівае палітычную і эклезіяльную супольнасці. Аўтар дапускае дапамогу ў надзвычайных абставінах, але яна не можа стаць пастаяннай заменай грамадзянскіх інстытутаў і іх уласнай адказнасці.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep the twofold acknowledgment of earthly autonomy and different spheres of competence as the basis for engagement with sciences and cultures; preserve the Church's own stated purpose in that engagement.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Прызнанне аўтаноміі і розных сфер кампетэнцыі адкрывае супрацоўніцтва з навукамі. Касцёл прапануе маральныя арыенціры і сам вучыцца развіваць сваё разуменне дзеля годнасці людзей, не прэтэндуючы на замену спецыяльных ведаў.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain the welcome offered to sincere seekers of truth, goodness and beauty, with scientific inquiry and diverse expert opinions; do not replace openness to debate with a claim that the Church settles empirical disputes.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Аўтар называе шчырых шукальнікаў праўды, дабра і прыгажосці саюзнікамі ў абароне годнасці. Давер да Аб’яўлення суіснуе з прызнаннем межаў уласнай кампетэнцыі і неабходнасцю сумленнай экспертнай дыскусіі з рознымі меркаваннямі.
qualificationChecks: Аўтар называе шчырых шукальнікаў праўды, дабра і прыгажосці саюзнікамі ў абароне годнасці. Давер да Аб’яўлення суіснуе з прызнаннем межаў уласнай кампетэнцыі і неабходнасцю сумленнай экспертнай дыскусіі з рознымі меркаваннямі.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Explain social teaching as discernment developed through Gospel and human knowledge, not a detached list of rules; its criteria concern persons, communities and the common good.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Сацыяльнае вучэнне развіваецца ў сустрэчы Евангелля з чалавечымі ведамі. Яго прынцыпы не адмяняюць вывучэння абставінаў: трэба адрозніваць тое, што сапраўды служыць асобам і супольнасцям, ад таго, што толькі называецца прагрэсам.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep truth as a shared gift and the warning against monopoly or prestige, including the polyhedron image for multiple perspectives; the source still claims one Gospel truth rather than relativism.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Разуменне праўды як дару супрацьстаіць яе манапалізацыі. Аўтар выкарыстоўвае вобраз шматгранніка: адзіная евангельская праўда можа быць выказана з розных перспектыў, а не праз падаўленне адрозненняў ці адзіны цэнтр улады.
qualificationChecks: Разуменне праўды як дару супрацьстаіць яе манапалізацыі. Аўтар выкарыстоўвае вобраз шматгранніка: адзіная евангельская праўда можа быць выказана з розных перспектыў, а не праз падаўленне адрозненняў ці адзіны цэнтр улады.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve cultural and historical plurality in the Church's account of catholicity; local contexts matter to application, even while the text maintains a universal vocation.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Паўсюднасць Касцёла ў аўтара не роўная аднастайнасці. Культурнае мноства патрабуе ўвагі да мясцовых праблем, бо менавіта ў канкрэтных умовах адбываюцца разуменне і ўвасабленне Евангелля.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep the contrast between a handbook and a living process of discernment, including dialogue, memory and prophecy; do not paraphrase the continuing presence of the Incarnate Word as merely institutional learning.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Сацыяльнае вучэнне прадстаўлена як працэс распазнавання, дыялогу і памяці, а не толькі збор правілаў. Аўтар звязвае гэты гістарычны шлях з працяглай прысутнасцю Уцелаўлёнага Слова і з адказнасцю перад новымі пытаннямі.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain the transition to selected stages since Rerum Novarum as a guide to the timeline; do not promise a comprehensive history beyond the overview the author supplies.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Пасля тлумачэння адносінаў Касцёла і свету аўтар пераходзіць да ключавых этапаў вучэння. Агляд ад Rerum novarum паказвае адказ на розныя гістарычныя выклікі, а не поўны каталог усіх дакументаў.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve the distinction between ancient Gospel reception and its modern systematization; the source does not describe social doctrine as spontaneously invented in the modern age.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Сучасная сацыяльная дактрына не ўзнікла з нічога: яна ўпарадкавала ранейшы досвед эклезіяльнага жыцця. Вернасць Евангеллю, паводле аўтара, дазваляе традыцыі адказваць на новыя падзеі, а не проста паўтараць мінулае.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep Rerum Novarum's worker dignity, association and wage concerns as the historical starting point; preserve its claim that evangelization has structural consequences rather than replacing it with a purely economic origin story.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Rerum novarum ставіць у цэнтр годнасць работнікаў і сацыяльнае пытанне індустрыялізацыі. Для аўтара абарона працы і сям’і паказвае, што евангелізацыя датычыць таксама грамадскіх структур, а не толькі прыватнай духоўнасці.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain Quadragesima Anno's criticism of both unlimited competition and collectivist suppression of personal responsibility, together with association and fair remuneration; the paired criticism prevents a one-sided political summary.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Quadragesima anno адказвае на эканамічны крызіс, канцэнтрацыю ўлады і несправядлівасць. Субсідыярнасць звязваецца з годнасцю працы, справядлівай аплатай і рэальнай магчымасцю сем’яў жыць годна, а не з простым змяншэннем дзяржавы.
qualificationChecks: Quadragesima anno адказвае на эканамічны крызіс, канцэнтрацыю ўлады і несправядлівасць. Субсідыярнасць звязваецца з годнасцю працы, справядлівай аплатай і рэальнай магчымасцю сем’яў жыць годна, а не з простым змяншэннем дзяржавы.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep Pius XII's war-and-reconstruction context, law over force, intermediary organizations and international imbalances; this is an attributed historical account, not a claim that all those institutions worked as intended.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Вучэнне Пія XII ў кантэксце вайны і аднаўлення падкрэслівае годнасць асобы і прававы парадак. Гэты ўнёсак аўтар звязвае з пазнейшым асэнсаваннем глабалізацыі і больш справядлівых адносінаў паміж народамі.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve John XXIII's widening global focus and rights-based institutions and relations between peoples; do not reduce the development to a change of papal personnel.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Ян XXIII разглядае сацыяльныя пытанні ў глабальным маштабе і праз правы чалавека. У інтэрпрэтацыі аўтара мір патрабуе не толькі добрых намераў, але і інстытутаў, абавязкаў і адносінаў, заснаваных на годнасці.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain Vatican II's turning point, human dignity and pluralistic peaceful societies; the historical explanation must keep the concrete rights criteria rather than just celebratory Council language.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Gaudium et spes звязвае жыццё Касцёла з радасцямі і пакутамі людзей. Павага да свабоды і сумлення, аўтаноміі грамадства і ўдзелу становіцца крытэрыем суіснавання ў плюралістычным свеце, з захаваннем рэлігійнай перспектывы Сабору.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep Paul VI's account of peace as more than the absence of war, linked to humane development and poorer countries; do not treat economic growth alone as the definition of peace.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Павел VI разглядае мір праз інтэгральнае развіццё кожнага чалавека і народа. Адсутнасць вайны недастатковая, калі захоўваюцца несправядлівыя адносіны, залежнасць і няроўны доступ да чалавечных умоў жыцця.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve Octogesima Adveniens' engagement with postindustrial change and exclusion; the historical application requires that no person or people be treated as expendable.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Octogesima adveniens пераносіць распазнаванне ў постіндустрыяльнае грамадства. Патрэбны мясцовы ўдзел і ўважлівая ацэнка абставінаў, каб ні асобы, ні народы не станавіліся расходным матэрыялам развіцця; хрысціянскія супольнасці самі нясуць за гэта адказнасць.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain John Paul II's treatment of work amid ideological crisis, sufficient remuneration and participation; labor's personal dignity is more than its usefulness to production.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Ян Павел II разглядае працу на фоне ідэалагічных крызісаў і глабалізацыі. Чалавек не можа быць толькі рэсурсам вытворчасці: патрэбны дастатковая аплата, права ўдзелу і грамадскія ўмовы, якія шануюць работніка.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep underdevelopment, responsibility and solidarity in Sollicitudo Rei Socialis; preserve the connection to political charity and civilization of love as the source's normative frame.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Sollicitudo rei socialis разглядае недастатковае развіццё і механізмы, што ўзнаўляюць несправядлівасць. Салідарнасць патрабуе адказнага выбару і перамены структур, а не толькі пачуцця спачування; аўтар звязвае яе з братэрствам і палітычнай любоўю.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain Centesimus Annus' reflection after the Soviet collapse together with continuing exploitation and representation crises; do not turn the passage into unconditional endorsement of whatever markets or democracies do.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Centesimus annus аналізуе крах савецкай сістэмы, дэмакратыю і рынкавую эканоміку. Абарона свабоды не адмяняе прававых і маральных межаў рынку, сацыяльнай адказнасці і крытыкі выключэння ды эксплуатацыі.
qualificationChecks: Centesimus annus аналізуе крах савецкай сістэмы, дэмакратыю і рынкавую эканоміку. Абарона свабоды не адмяняе прававых і маральных межаў рынку, сацыяльнай адказнасці і крытыкі выключэння ды эксплуатацыі.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep Benedict XVI's widening of development and the political community's irreplaceable responsibility; this limits a reading in which growth alone or private generosity supplies the common good.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Caritas in veritate пашырае разуменне развіцця па-за матэрыяльны рост. Эканоміку і тэхналогіі належыць ацэньваць праз агульнае дабро, а палітычная супольнасць захоўвае ўласную адказнасць, якую нельга цалкам перадаць рынку.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve charity joined to truth and its critical public role; the text does not define charity as private sentiment detached from institutions or justice.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Бэнэдыкт XVI называе любоў галоўным шляхам сацыяльнага вучэння пры яе сувязі з праўдай. Аўтар разглядае яе як стваральную грамадскую сілу, якая патрабуе справядлівых інстытутаў і палітыкі, а не толькі прыватнай дабрачыннасці.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep Francis' account of history through hopes and vulnerabilities and the Church's learning from the poor; the poor are participants in the institution's transformation, not merely recipients.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Францішак развівае саборнае бачанне гісторыі праз канкрэтных людзей і іх пакуты. У аўтара евангелізацыя ідзе разам са слуханнем бедных: супольнасць не толькі навучае, але і дазваляе досведу іншых яе змяняць.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain integral ecology and the criticism of self-referential politics and finance in Laudato Si'; preserve the source's systemic connection between environmental and social harms.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Laudato si’ паказвае экалагічны крызіс як частку сацыяльнага пытання. Аўтар звязвае клопат пра стварэнне з жыццём бедных, адказнасцю гаспадаркі і палітыкі і дыялогам паміж імі, замест ізаляваных тэхнічных рашэнняў.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep Fratelli Tutti's response to fragmentation, conflict and pandemic in the account of fraternity; its broad social friendship must not be narrowed to the author's own religious group.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: На фоне войнаў, індывідуалізму і пандэміі Францішак падкрэслівае братэрства і сацыяльную дружбу. Для аўтара гэта заклік аднаўляць сувязі паміж людзьмі і адказваць любоўю, а не задавальняцца фармальнай узаемазалежнасцю.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Retain the conclusion that social teaching responds to concrete history while preserving an internal core; the overview invites attention to coherence, not a claim that no historical tensions exist.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Гістарычны агляд паказвае цярплівае развіццё вучэння ў сустрэчы з рэальнасцю. Яго адзінства не азначае адсутнасці змен: аўтар прапануе правяраць, як прынцыпы разам дзейнічаюць у асабістым і грамадскім жыцці.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Introduce the principles as interrelated within a living teaching in dialogue with history, cultures and sciences; individual concept cards must not imply that each principle stands alone.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Сацыяльныя прынцыпы трэба разглядаць разам: іх сэнс раскрываецца ва ўзаемным дапаўненні. Жывы дыялог з гісторыяй, культурамі і навукамі не адмяняе ядра перакананняў, якое Касцёл захоўвае.
qualificationChecks: Сацыяльныя прынцыпы трэба разглядаць разам: іх сэнс раскрываецца ва ўзаемным дапаўненні. Жывы дыялог з гісторыяй, культурамі і навукамі не адмяняе ядра перакананняў, якое Касцёл захоўвае.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve the different responsibilities of lay people and pastoral leaders for just social life; identify the original religious audience while making the duties legible without silently changing who is addressed.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Аўтар звяртаецца да свецкіх вернікаў і людзей добрай волі: сацыяльная адказнасць патрабуе распазнавання, а не толькі згоды з прынцыпамі. Мэта — больш справядлівае і братэрскае жыццё.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep the Trinity as the stated source of received and shared love in optional foundations; it is a theological premise, not another name for interpersonal cooperation.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Аўтар выводзіць сацыяльнае вучэнне з веры ў Бога як камунію Айца, Сына і Духа. Чалавек у гэтым бачанні пакліканы прымаць любоў і дзяліцца ёю; сацыяльныя сувязі маюць не толькі інструментальны сэнс.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve the Incarnation and Spirit-led life as the Christian grounding of social consequences; moving this explanation to foundations must not imply that the ethical claims had no religious basis.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: У Езусе Хрысце аўтар бачыць канкрэтнае ўвасабленне Божай любові. Адносіны, якія вера адкрывае ў Уцелаўленні і дзеянні Духа, павінны мець наступствы для грамадства, а не заставацца выключна ўнутраным рэлігійным досведам.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep being created in God's image as the source's account of personhood and the person as the Church's way; retain that rationale separately from the secular statement of unconditional worth.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: У разуменні Льва XIV годнасць не залежыць ад здольнасцяў, багацця, становішча або маральнага поспеху. Асобу нельга прымусіць спачатку заслужыць права на павагу.

protectedSpans.text: У аснове хрысціянскага разумення чалавечай асобы ляжыць вялікае біблійнае сцвярджэнне, што мужчыны і жанчыны створаны на вобраз і падабенства Бога (пар. Быц 1, 26-27), Адзінага ў Тройцы. Створаны дзеля адносінаў, кожны чалавек задуманы і жаданы Богам, каб увайсці ў камунію з Ім, з іншымі і са стварэннем. Годнасць чалавека не залежыць ад яго здольнасцяў, багацця і жыццёвага становішча, ад правільнага ці няправільнага выбару: гэта Божы дар, які апярэджвае і пераўзыходзіць асобу, выраз Яго любові, якая ніколі не мінае. Таму чалавек назаўсёды застаецца «дарогай Касцёла» [55] і сэрцам кожнага сапраўднага шляху інтэгральнага чалавечага развіцця [56].

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve the transition from uniqueness and dignity to rights inherent in being human; the authority cited is John Paul II and the Church's teaching, not an unqualified legal claim about every jurisdiction.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Павага да непаўторнасці асобы і яе сумлення вымагае правоў, якія не выдаюцца як узнагарода. Чалавечая ўлада не можа адвольна адмяняць або абмяжоўваць годнасць і правы людзей.
qualificationChecks: Павага да непаўторнасці асобы і яе сумлення вымагае правоў, якія не выдаюцца як узнагарода. Чалавечая ўлада не можа адвольна адмяняць або абмяжоўваць годнасць і правы людзей.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Define moral, social, existential and ontological dignity separately; the first three can vary while intrinsic worth cannot be diminished, with creation and divine love retained as the optional grounding.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Маральная годнасць датычыць учынкаў, сацыяльная — умоў і павагі, экзістэнцыяльная — перажывання ўласнай каштоўнасці. Яны могуць змяняцца; анталагічная годнасць, паводле аўтара, належыць праз існаванне і не губляецца праз грэх, няўдачу або выключэнне.
qualificationChecks: Маральная годнасць датычыць учынкаў, сацыяльная — умоў і павагі, экзістэнцыяльная — перажывання ўласнай каштоўнасці. Яны могуць змяняцца; анталагічная годнасць, паводле аўтара, належыць праз існаванне і не губляецца праз грэх, няўдачу або выключэнне. Аўтар адрознівае маральную годнасць, якая датычыць учынкаў, сацыяльную — умоў жыцця і павагі, і экзістэнцыяльную — перажывання каштоўнасці сябе і жыцця. Гэтыя тры вымярэнні могуць узрастаць або змяншацца. Анталагічная годнасць належыць кожнай асобе праз існаванне і не памяншаецца праз грэх, няўдачу, прыніжэнне або дыскрымінацыю. Аўтар абгрунтоўвае яе тым, што чалавека жадае, стварае і любіць Бог; гэта не адмяняе адказнасці за ўчынкі і неабходнасці выпраўляць несправядлівыя ўмовы.

protectedSpans.text: Калі мы гаворым пра годнасць, мы не заўсёды выкарыстоўваем гэтае слова ў аднолькавым значэнні. Часам мы маем на ўвазе маральную годнасць, а менавіта, на што арыентуецца чалавек у сваім выбары і дзейнасці. Іншым разам мы думаем пра сацыяльную годнасць, якая датычыць умоў жыцця чалавека і канкрэтнай пашаны, якую атрымлівае ад грамадства. У іншых выпадках мы маем на ўвазе экзістэнцыяльную годнасць, гэта значыць тое, як чалавек успрымае каштоўнасць самога сябе і каштоўнасць жыцця. Гэтыя аспекты годнасці могуць узрастаць або змяншацца. Акрамя гэтых паняццяў, існуе таксама больш глыбокі і важны ўзровень анталагічнай годнасці. Гэта годнасць, якая належыць кожнай асобе праз сам факт існавання, проста таму, што яе жадаў, стварыў і палюбіў Бог [60]. Ніякі грэх, няўдача, прыніжэнне або дыскрымінацыя не могуць паменшыць непарушнай каштоўнасці чалавечага жыцця, якога захацеў Бог і якое паклікаў да існавання [61].

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep the claim that fundamental dignity is not earned or extinguished, even by moral failure; attribute its foundation and resist turning other kinds of diminished dignity into diminished human worth.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Фундаментальная годнасць не набываецца і не патрабуе доказу ўласнай карыснасці. Аўтар сцвярджае яе нават там, дзе чалавек не можа дзейнічаць або адчувае сябе нікчэмным.
qualificationChecks: Фундаментальная годнасць не набываецца і не патрабуе доказу ўласнай карыснасці. Аўтар сцвярджае яе нават там, дзе чалавек не можа дзейнічаць або адчувае сябе нікчэмным. Фундаментальная годнасць, паводле аўтара, не набываецца і не патрабуе заслуг або доказу сваёй карыснасці. Dignitas infinita звязвае яе з безумоўнай Божай любоўю: не існуе такой умовы або працягласці пошуку, якая магла б сцерці каштоўнасць асобы. Гэта атрыбутаванае рэлігійнае абгрунтаванне непарушнасці, а не мера здольнасцяў чалавека.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Preserve gratitude for the historical identification of rights and the duty of international protection; rights are concrete expressions of intrinsic dignity, not merely a list of admired aspirations.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Касцёл прызнае значэнне міжнароднага абвяшчэння правоў чалавека. Але іх аснова, у разуменні аўтара, не зводзіцца да рашэння арганізацыі: яны выражаюць унутраную годнасць, якую супольнасць павінна абараняць.

sourceComparisons.meaningCheck: Keep universal rights and the source's explicit life-from-conception-to-natural-end position, including abortion and euthanasia, through clear Church attribution; secular navigation must not erase contested normative commitments.
sourceComparisons.qualifiedSummary: Паводле Касцёла, правы ўніверсальныя і неад’емныя, а іх абвяшчэнне патрабуе рэальнай абароны ўсіх. Аўтар называе першым права на жыццё ад зачацця да натуральнай смерці і захоўвае адмоўную пазіцыю Касцёла адносна аборту, забойства нявінных і эўтаназіі.
qualificationChecks: Паводле Касцёла, правы ўніверсальныя і неад’емныя, а іх абвяшчэнне патрабуе рэальнай абароны ўсіх. Аўтар называе першым права на жыццё ад зачацця да натуральнай смерці і захоўвае адмоўную пазіцыю Касцёла адносна аборту, забойства нявінных і эўтаназіі.
